Founded by a Shell veteran with nine years of global oil‑marketing experience, MyPetrolPump operates out of Bengaluru, Karnataka, and serves the B2B supply‑chain and logistics sector. With a team of 42, it has been acquired, marking its success in addressing a critical infrastructure gap in India.

startups.title: Gaiascope
startups.description: SaaS that helps renewables & energy storage operate more profitably. YC S19.
startups.prose:
**Website:** http://gaia-scope.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/gaiascope

Gaiascope offers a SaaS platform that simplifies electric grid forecasting and operations for hard assets such as wind, solar, and energy storage.
The software delivers timely, unbiased information that helps these assets improve revenues, reduce risk, and maximize the profitability of every megawatt.
In addition to its core product, Gaiascope manages a quant fund that trades electricity, using the fund’s performance to build credibility with clients and accelerate continuous improvement of its software. The company was acquired.

startups.title: SolarMente
startups.description: Home electrification at $0 upfront cost. YC S21.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://solarmente.es | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/solarmente

SolarMente enabled homeowners in Southern Europe to install solar panels, energy storage, and heat pumps with zero upfront cost. The company operated on a model where users paid through predictable monthly savings rather than a large initial capital expenditure. Based in Barcelona with a team of 65, SolarMente raised $5M from investors including Y Combinator, Climate Capital, and Leonardo DiCaprio. The company has since become inactive.

startups.title: Nabis
startups.description: Nabis operates the largest licensed cannabis wholesale platform in California. YC W19.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.nabis.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/nabis

Nabis is the #1 licensed cannabis wholesaling platform in California, distributing over $1 billion of cannabis annually and supporting more than 500 exclusive brands. It supplies the entire network of state‑licensed dispensaries with top‑tier products.

The company provides lightning‑fast fulfillment, warehousing, payment processing, financing, data analytics, and sales and marketing services, enabling brands and retailers to innovate, launch, and scale. With a team of 700 and headquarters in New York City, Nabis combines B2B supply‑chain expertise with fintech capabilities to streamline the cannabis market.

startups.title: TrueMile
startups.description: An AI-operated logistics company. YC F26.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://TrueMile.AI/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/truemile

TrueMile is building a fully autonomous logistics company, starting with trucking. Delayed pickups, empty miles and poor planning eat into a carrier's profits. Its agents coordinate loads, routes, driver schedules and fuel stops to earn more from each truck and lower the cost of moving goods.

TrueMile is starting with its own fleet so it controls execution, learn from every delivery and keep the gains. Human drivers come first. As autonomous trucks become available on its routes, it will have the customers, freight and infrastructure ready for them.

As it drives toward AGI, people will still need groceries, clothes and materials to build their homes. Someone has to move all of it. It wants every leap in AI to show up in what people pay for everyday goods.

startups.title: Parrot
startups.description: TikTok for language learning. YC F25.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://parrotapp.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/parrot

Parrot is the TikTok for language learning. Parrot turns doomscrolling into fluency with personalized short-form videos. Power users scroll for 6 hours/week on Parrot. Its team of engineers have lived the frustration of ineffective apps and learning methods - we’re building the first language platform that actually works.

startups.title: Doomersion
startups.description: Doomscroll to learn languages. YC W26.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://doomersion.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/doomersion

Doomersion lets you learn languages by doomscrolling. Watch TikToks in your target language matched exactly to your current level — as you scroll, they get slightly harder. Gen-Z doomscrolls 2.5–3 hours a day; if you bake immersion into that with viral videos in another language matched to their level, you get the optimal language learning method.

Gained ~15,000 downloads in the first two weeks. Power users spend 3+ hours daily on the app.

startups.title: Strive School
startups.description: Training European STEM students into job-ready software engineers via a six-month online program. YC S20.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://strive.school | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/strive-school

Strive School operates a six-month online program designed to transform STEM students into professional-grade software engineers. The company addresses the gap between theoretical university curricula and industry requirements by providing practical, job-ready training for those pursuing science and technology fields in Europe.

The platform utilizes an income share agreement model, where students pay a portion of their future salary in exchange for access to the curriculum. This approach allows candidates to defer costs until they are employed, aligning the company's success with the career outcomes of its graduates.

Strive School was acquired, marking a significant milestone for the Berlin-based team. The company, which maintains a small remote-first team, focused on the intersection of education and fintech to modernize software engineering training in the European market.

startups.title: Safer Management
startups.description: Attendance tracking software for public schools and colleges. YC S21.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.safermgmt.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/safer-management

Safer Management provides attendance tracking software to public school districts and colleges. The platform addresses the financial incentive for public schools to maintain high average daily attendance, which directly impacts their federal funding.

Founded in Dallas, Texas, the company was launched after the founder observed inefficiencies in the sign-in process while dropping off his children. The team has since expanded to serve 75 public schools and two colleges, generating annual recurring revenue of $621,000 with 82% margins. The company is currently profitable and operates on a pricing model that scales to $15 per student per year.

Safer Management targets a market of 70 million public school students in the United States, representing a $1.4 billion opportunity. The company utilizes artificial intelligence and machine learning tags to support its operations within the education sector.

startups.title: Goodkind
startups.description: Student communications platform for higher education. YC S21.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.goodkind.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/goodkind

Goodkind provides a student communications platform designed for universities and colleges. It enables institutions to engage with their student bodies through multiple channels, including SMS, video, chat, and mail.

The company operated as a B2B SaaS provider based in Toronto, Canada, with a team of approximately 30 people. It was part of the Summer 2021 Y Combinator batch.

Goodkind has since been acquired, marking the exit of this higher-ed focused communication tool from the independent startup landscape.

startups.title: Taro
startups.description: A community and hiring platform connecting high-growth tech companies with top software engineers. YC S22.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://joinTaro.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/taro

Taro operates as a community of over 150,000 software engineers focused on career growth, serving as a talent pipeline for high-growth technology companies. The platform combines an education component, featuring online courses and discussions with leaders at top tech firms, with direct hiring support that includes sourcing and feedback on candidates.

Based in San Francisco, Taro was acquired, marking a significant milestone for this YC Summer 2022 startup. Its approach distinguishes itself by leveraging educational content to attract engineers who are actively seeking their next career move, thereby helping startups expand their engineering teams quickly without compromising on quality.

startups.title: Acely
startups.description: Acely provides an AI-powered tutor for the digital SAT and ACT to help students prepare for college admissions. YC W18.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://acely.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/acely

Acely is the leading AI tutor for the digital SAT and ACT, helping students gain confidence and improve their chances of admission to their dream college. Backed by Forerunner Ventures, the company has reached $10M ARR and operates with a 30‑person team based in San Francisco. Acely launched out of beta in January 2024 as a spinout product from Juni, a YC W18 company, and continues to scale its AI‑native tools for high‑school families.

startups.title: SharpestMinds
startups.description: SharpestMinds runs peer-to-peer data-science mentorships funded by income-share agreements. YC W18.
startups.prose:
**Website:** http://sharpestminds.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/sharpestminds

SharpestMinds operates a mentorship program for aspiring data scientists that pairs them with experienced engineers. The mentors, drawn from leading AI groups at Apple, Uber, Tesla, Facebook and Amazon, guide mentees through real-world projects and interview preparation. Mentees join the program at no upfront cost and agree to pay a percentage of their first-year salary after they are hired, aligning the program's revenue with the success of its graduates. The model functions as a talent-matching service that blends education with recruiting. SharpestMinds was acquired after its Winter 2018 Y Combinator batch. The company, based in Toronto with remote staff and a four-person team, operates in the B2B recruiting and talent space.

startups.title: Edwin
startups.description: Edwin provides an AI‑powered virtual English tutor delivering personalized 1:1 learning. YC W18.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://edwin.ai | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/edwin

Edwin combines adaptive learning and natural language understanding technology with pedagogical content and on‑demand human instructors to offer affordable, personalized 1:1 English tutoring. Based in San Francisco, the startup was backed by General Catalyst, Y Combinator, the Google Assistant Investments Program and other investors, and has helped over 800 000 students improve their English.

In early 2020 Edwin merged with MyBuddy.ai, and the combined entity kept the Buddy.ai name. The new company focuses on a voice‑based English conversation partner for the roughly 500 million children worldwide who need practice speaking the language, extending the mobile Buddy app that blends solutions from both original firms.

Edwin’s status is listed as Acquired, reflecting its consolidation into Buddy.ai.

startups.title: Glimpse K12
startups.description: Glimpse K12 captures school activities and evaluates them against student achievement to maximize education ROI. YC W18.
startups.prose:
**Website:** http://www.glimpsek12.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/glimpse-k12

Glimpse K12 captures everything a district does to impact student outcomes and evaluates those activities in the context of student achievement. By turning otherwise opaque education return on investment (eROI) into measurable data, the company helps schools align time and money with the unique needs of their students.

The platform provides answers to critical questions that traditionally make eROI virtually impossible to track and manage, thereby eliminating ineffective spending in schools. Glimpse K12 was acquired, reflecting the value of its analytics approach in the education sector.

The company operates with a team of six out of Huntsville, Alabama.

startups.title: FunctionUp (FanPlay)
startups.description: A technical placement bootcamp that trains talent with zero upfront fees and places them at partner companies. YC W21.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.functionup.org/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/functionup-fanplay

FunctionUp, also known as FanPlay, operates a skill-tech platform focused on technical placement bootcamps. The company utilizes an Income Sharing Model, allowing it to train top tech talent without charging any upfront fees. Upon completion of the program, graduates are placed across the company's network of partner companies.

Based in Bengaluru, India, FunctionUp combines technical training with a strong social impact mission. The program provides specific assistance to women and unemployed youth in India, supporting them both economically and socially. The company was part of the Y Combinator Winter 2021 batch and has since been acquired.

startups.title: Mathos
startups.description: Mathos delivers an AI math problem solver that boosts student performance and teacher productivity. YC W24.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://info.mathos.ai/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/mathos

Mathos is a leading AI math solver that helps students and teachers improve academic performance and productivity. The platform has served over 1 million students in more than 200 countries this past year, turning personalized learning from a mission‑impossible goal into a reality.

Its advanced math model outperforms GPT‑4o by roughly 20 % in mathematical and quantitative problem‑solving accuracy. The company is tackling the hardest challenges in education, including personalization, adaptive learning, and teacher shortages, with trial runs underway in schools.

By automating grading, delivering insightful analytics, and generating adaptive assignments, Mathos empowers teachers to understand what their students need and to provide the right support. The startup remains active and headquartered in San Francisco.

startups.title: Alice.tech
startups.description: Alice.tech provides AI‑driven personalized exam preparation for college students. YC W25.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.alice.tech/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/alice-tech

Alice.tech turns generic course materials into personalized learning and exam preparation using AI. The service is described as “Duolingo for exams” and has already been used by more than 10 k college students.

The Copenhagen‑based startup reports $20 k in monthly recurring revenue and a 10 % week‑over‑week growth rate over the past eight weeks. With a team of five, it targets a core market opportunity of over $10 b within the nearly $10 trillion global education market, betting on AI‑driven disruption and product virality.

startups.title: Vidcode
startups.description: Vidcode offers self-guided coding courses for tweens and teens. YC S16.
startups.prose:
**Website:** http://vidcode.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/vidcode

Vidcode provides computer science courses for tweens and teens, featuring more than three hundred self‑guided tutorials that teach web development fundamentals. The curricular approach lets students build video filters, simulations, augmented reality, and other creative projects while learning core programming concepts. Founded by female developers and artists, the company was originally built with girls in mind and focuses on increasing participation from young women and underrepresented minorities. Vidcode was acquired.

startups.title: Eduflow
startups.description: Eduflow builds software to create and run active, collaborative online learning experiences. YC S17.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.eduflow.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/eduflow

Eduflow provides a platform designed to host active online learning experiences. Rather than relying on passive video playlists, the software enables instructors to build interactive learning activities that make students active participants in their own education process.

Based in Copenhagen, Denmark, Eduflow was used across thousands of institutions worldwide, spanning from middle school classrooms to corporate training programs at companies like Google. The company participated in the Y Combinator Summer 2017 batch with a team of 12 and has since been acquired.

startups.title: Mystery.org
startups.description: Mystery.org creates engaging video explanations for children’s science questions. YC S17.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://mystery.org | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/mystery-org

Mystery.org began by compiling the 150 most common science questions children ask teachers, forming its Mystery Science collection. The platform reached more than 4 million children in 50 % of U.S. elementary schools, and it has sold thousands of schools without employing a single salesperson. Backed by Y Combinator, Learn Capital, and Reach Capital, the company has expanded its scope to answer all other questions children have, receiving over 500 k inquiries in the last 18 months and producing video explanations for each.

The company’s mission is to cultivate a generation of better thinkers by providing clear, visual explanations—essentially a visual Wikipedia for kids. Mystery.org was acquired in 2024, marking its success in the education sector.

startups.title: Py
startups.description: Py democratizes access to career opportunities in tech. YC S17.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.getpy.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/py

Py offers iOS and Android apps that deliver millions of lessons and quizzes, modernizing traditional online teaching tools.
The company launched Py for Work, a platform that lets companies assess candidates with real-world assessments instead of brain teasers, helping industry leaders such as LiveRamp, Amplitude, and Factual hire based on merit.
Py was acquired.
The team of three is based in San Francisco, CA, and the company operates in the education sector with a focus on recruiting.

startups.title: Demand Curve
startups.description: Demand Curve is a growth operating system that teaches startups how to build scalable growth engines. YC S19.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.demandcurve.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/demand-curve

Demand Curve offers a membership and course that guides startup operators through building a growth engine without hiring a full team. The program is powered by a premium content library, expert guidance, and an AI growth co‑pilot that walks users through each step. In addition to the program, Demand Curve publishes a weekly Growth Newsletter that reaches more than 100,000 founders and marketers, boasting a 46‑50% open rate. The company also runs a full‑service agency that has helped scale Microsoft, Framer, Pilot, Ancestry, and hundreds of other YC startups.

startups.title: Blair
startups.description: Blair financed education through income share agreements. YC S19.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://joinblair.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/blair

Blair is a fintech company that financed education through income share agreements. The company raised a $100M debt fund and $7.5M in equity from top‑tier VCs and multiple unicorn founders. Blair sold all of its assets in 2022 after regulatory changes in the space and has since become inactive.

startups.title: Scrimba
startups.description: Scrimba turns people into hireable devs for 1% of the price of code. YC S20.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://scrimba.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/scrimba

Scrimba is a coding course platform that hosts interactive screencasts, engaging over 120K monthly active students.

The platform’s new video format makes screencasts fully interactive for students, allowing them to run and edit code directly while watching, and it simplifies content creation for teachers.

With a vision to combine Stanford‑level quality with gym‑membership pricing, Scrimba aims to democratize software education from its base in Oslo, Norway, with a lean team of six.

startups.title: StudyStream
startups.description: A 24/7 video platform and online community enabling students from over 180 countries to study together in real time. YC S21.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://studystream.live | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/studystream

StudyStream operates a video platform and online community designed to help students study collaboratively in real time, available around the clock. By connecting learners from over 180 countries, the platform aims to reduce isolation and boost productivity through peer accountability and motivation.

The company has supported more than 3 million students in becoming more productive and motivated. Based in London with a remote-friendly team of eight, StudyStream focuses on building a global community where students can encourage one another to succeed.

startups.title: Our World in Data
startups.description: Our World in Data provides free, open-source visualizations and research on global challenges. YC W19.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://ourworldindata.org/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/our-world-in-data

Our World in Data publishes an open-access platform that lets users explore the state of the world through interactive data visualizations and summaries of scientific literature. It covers topics ranging from global poverty and health to climate change and education, offering 3405 charts across 297 topics.

The service is free, open-source, and positioned as a public good, attracting millions of monthly users and frequent citations in research and media worldwide. With a team of 19 located in Oxford and remote, it operates in the education sector as a nonprofit organization.

The organization remains active, continuously adding new visualizations to help people understand progress and setbacks on the world’s largest problems.

startups.title: Icarus
startups.description: Stratospheric solar drones for defense intelligence. YC F25.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.icarus.one | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/icarus

Icarus is building the modern-day U-2 spy plane. Autonomous solar aircraft fly at 60,000 feet for weeks at a time — above weather and below satellites — delivering persistent intelligence and connectivity for the military at a fraction of the cost of existing systems.

The stratosphere is the forgotten frontier: above commercial air traffic, below satellites, and currently essentially unoccupied. Team of 50. Los Angeles. The defense application is ISR (Intelligence, Surveillance, Reconnaissance) at dramatically lower cost than traditional satellites.

startups.title: Tornyol
startups.description: Tornyol builds micro-drones that kill mosquitoes. YC F25.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://tornyol.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/tornyol

Tornyol builds micro-drones that kill mosquitoes. Tornyol uses smartphone microphones, car park assist sensors and some clever DSP and control to transform 40-gram toy drones into mosquito killers. Because these drones are so cheap and fast, it wills lower the cost of mosquito control by 100x which will enable the eradication of mosquitoes from cities, saving more than a million people each year from Malaria, West Nile, Dengue, etc.

startups.title: Milliray
startups.description: Technology to detect and track small drones. YC W26.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://milliray.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/milliray

Milliray makes radars that can see small drones.

As drones evolve faster than air defenses, detection has fallen behind. Even $50 drones now present a major threat to airports, critical infrastructure, and front-line defense.

It solves this by building high-frequency radar systems, designed from the ground up to detect even the most challenging low-signature targets. This allows us to identify and track nano drones like no other solution, letting you know what's truly in your airspace.

startups.title: GRU Space
startups.description: First commercial lunar hotel — taking reservations for stays on the Moon. YC W26.
startups.prose:
Founded solo by [Skyler Chan](./Skyler%20Chan.md), age 22. Currently accepting reservations at $250K–$1M per stay. The only YC company in the W26 batch building commercial lunar hospitality infrastructure.

GRU Space's thesis: the Moon will have permanent human presence within a decade (via NASA's Artemis program, SpaceX, and commercial partners), and the hospitality infrastructure — safe, comfortable, commercially operated habitats — is a separate problem from the rocket and lander problem that governments and large primes are solving.

The business model mirrors early commercial aviation: sell experiences to wealthy early adopters, use that revenue to fund infrastructure that eventually enables broader access. The $250K–$1M price point targets the same customer who buys a Virgin Galactic ticket, not the general public.

At YC demo day, GRU Space had the highest novelty premium of the batch — the kind of audacious bet that generates coverage regardless of near-term revenue. Whether it's viable depends entirely on the pace of lunar infrastructure development from SpaceX and NASA.

startups.title: Fed10
startups.description: AI Agents for Government Affairs. YC W26.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.fed10.ai | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fed10

Fed10 is a legislative consulting firm staffed by AI agents.

Fed10 monitors every bill across the U.S., flag threats to your business, and deliver actionable insights — the same work a $500/hr policy consultant does, but in seconds instead of days.

Built by three ex-lobbyists who passed legislation together.

startups.title: 9 Mothers
startups.description: Developing low-cost, autonomous counter-drone systems for defense applications. YC Sp26.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://9mothers.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/9-mothers-corporation

9 Mothers is a defense technology company based in Austin, Texas, that specializes in counter-drone systems. The company has sold $1.6 million worth of systems to the Department of War, delivering multiple units to the agency. Its flagship product, EDDA, is a small, low-power, and low-cost system designed to be deployed on vehicles, bases, or carried by personnel to intercept Group 1 suicide drones.

With a team of 19, 9 Mothers has secured multiple contracts and sales for its autonomous-capable hardware. Beyond its initial product, the company is developing three additional systems that are currently in various stages of development to meet ongoing demand in the defense sector.

startups.title: Seneca Systems
startups.description: Constituent system-of-record and service request management software for government. YC S16.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.senecagov.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/seneca-systems

Seneca Systems developed Romulus, a Constituent Services Platform designed to centralize communications and organize service requests for government teams. The software addresses the challenges of managing constituent interactions across multiple channels by providing visibility into public opinions and the work performed by government employees.

The company aimed to replace outdated private-sector software with a solution built specifically for government workflows, enabling workers to handle requests with less overhead. Seneca Systems was acquired.

startups.title: Flock Safety
startups.description: A public safety operating system using AI-powered devices to help law enforcement eliminate crime. YC S17.
startups.prose:
**Website:** http://www.flocksafety.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/flock-safety

Flock Safety provides a public safety operating system that empowers private communities and law enforcement to collaborate in eliminating crime. The company offers a Safety-as-a-Service model featuring affordable, LTE and solar-powered devices that can be installed anywhere to detect and capture objective details. These devices decode evidence in real-time and deliver investigative leads directly to relevant public servants.

Headquartered in Atlanta with a team of approximately 1,000 employees, Flock Safety operates nationwide. The company emphasizes ethical design to protect human privacy and mitigate bias in policing. It raised $150M in a Series E round led by Tiger Global at a $3.5B valuation.

startups.title: Elucd
startups.description: Elucd provides cities with near real-time insight into how citizens feel about their government. YC S17.
startups.prose:
**Website:** http://www.elucd.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/elucd

Elucd is a GovTech SaaS platform that uses mobile ad polling to give cities near real-time insight into citizen sentiment about their government.

Founded in the Summer 2017 batch, the company operated out of New York City with a team of eight.

Elucd was acquired, marking its success in the GovTech space.

startups.title: Momentus
startups.description: Momentus provides space infrastructure services using water plasma propulsion to enable cost-effective in-space transport. YC S18.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://momentus.space | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/momentus

Momentus is a space infrastructure services company that positions itself as a first mover, offering foundational services that enable businesses to flourish in space.
With an experienced team of aerospace, propulsion, and robotics engineers, Momentus designs and operates cost‑effective and energy‑efficient in‑space transport and service vehicles that utilize water plasma propulsion technology.
The company has secured service agreements with numerous private satellite operators, government agencies, and research organizations, and it is a public company.

startups.title: Phiar
startups.description: Phiar builds the first AI-powered AR navigation software that runs entirely on a smartphone and in-vehicle displays. YC S18.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.phiar.net | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/phiar

Phiar develops the first AI-powered AR navigation software for driving that runs on smartphones and in-vehicle displays, leveraging an ultra‑lightweight road‑understanding AI that operates entirely at the edge in real time.

The platform is designed to enhance driving safety, provide intuitive wayfinding, and connect drivers with their surrounding environments. It was founded in Summer 2018 and has a team of 12 based in San Francisco and Redwood City.

Phiar was acquired, marking its recognition as a notable player in automotive AI and augmented reality.

startups.title: Ramen VR
startups.description: Ramen VR transforms game development with advanced XR + AI tools. YC S19.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://ramenvr.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/ramen-vr

Ramen VR is a San Francisco‑based studio that builds XR and AI tools for creators of online games and virtual worlds, building on its success with the #1 VR game Zenith: The Last City on Steam and Quest. The company has raised over $40 million and is working stealth on a new game and a suite of tools designed to shape the future of game development. With a team of 15 developers spread across San Francisco and El Cerrito, Ramen VR focuses on empowering developers to build meaningful games that can change lives.

startups.title: Turion Space
startups.description: Building dual-use spacecraft for space domain awareness imaging and orbital debris removal. YC S21.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://turionspace.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/turion-space

Turion Space is developing dual-use spacecraft technology designed to move objects in space and image them when they are not being moved. The company, which operates out of Los Angeles and Irvine with a team of 15, focuses on creating a sustainable future in space by advancing affordable solutions for orbital debris removal.

The founding team, which originates from SpaceX, participated in the Y Combinator accelerator in Summer 2021. Following the program, Turion Space raised a $6.2M seed round to support its mission.

The company aims to establish a foundation by selling space domain awareness imagery data while progressing toward asteroid mining capabilities. Its first DROID satellite was scheduled to launch in early 2023.

startups.title: Instacrops
startups.description: Instacrops provides IoT sensors and satellite analytics to help farmers in Latin America maximize crop yields. YC S21.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.instacrops.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/instacrops

Instacrops operates a dashboard platform that combines data from IoT sensors, satellites, and drones to provide detailed analytics on farm health. The company is headquartered in Santiago, Chile, and employs a team of 34 people focused on bringing data-driven decision-making to the agricultural sector.

The platform is currently live on more than 300 farms across Latin America, where it has helped farmers increase their crop yields by an average of 12%. Instacrops has reached over $200,000 in monthly revenue with growth rates of 2X year-over-year.

The company targets the $50 billion agricultural market in Latin America, which encompasses 2.9 billion acres of farmland. By integrating physical hardware with remote sensing data, Instacrops aims to optimize farming operations across the region.

startups.title: Shiok Meats
startups.description: Shiok Meats produces cell‑based shrimp and other seafood without raising animals. YC W19.
startups.prose:
**Website:** http://www.shiokmeats.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/shiok-meats

Shiok Meats is a cell‑based clean meat company that focuses exclusively on seafood. Based in Singapore, it uses cellular agriculture to grow shrimp and other marine protein in a laboratory from animal cells, eliminating the need for animal farming. The company describes its products as animal‑, health‑ and environment‑friendly, offering the same taste, texture and nutrients as conventional shrimp while avoiding cruelty.

Shiok Meats is the first cell‑based meat company in Singapore and Southeast Asia, positioning it as a regional pioneer in cultivated seafood. The company has a nine‑person team operating out of Singapore and was acquired, reflecting investor confidence in its approach to climate‑friendly protein production.

startups.title: Atomic Alchemy
startups.description: Atomic Alchemy builds privately-owned nuclear reactors to produce medical radioisotopes. YC W19.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://atomicalchemy.us | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/atomic-alchemy

Atomic Alchemy is constructing a bank of small modular reactors that will serve as a dedicated, scalable facility for producing radioisotopes used in nuclear medicine, such as the Molybdenum‑99 needed for diagnostics and cancer treatments. The current global supply of Molybdenum‑99 relies on six aging, government‑run research reactors abroad, five of which are 45‑65 years old, creating a fragile and lengthy supply chain.

By creating the world’s first privately‑owned reactors focused on isotope production, Atomic Alchemy aims to shorten lead times and enable more reliable access to materials for clinical trials and treatments. The company, based in Idaho Falls, ID with a team of eight, was acquired, reflecting the strategic value of its hard‑tech approach to medical device supply.

startups.title: Impactive (formerly Outvote)
startups.description: Provides a distributed organizing and peer-to-peer texting platform for progressive political campaigns and advocacy causes. YC S18.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.impactive.io/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/impactive

Impactive, originally founded in 2017 as Outvote with support from Y Combinator and Higher Ground Labs, developed a distributed organizing platform for political and civic campaigns. Initially created as a get-out-the-vote tool for Democrats, the product grew into a full-service suite that allows progressive causes, campaigns, and nonprofits to engage supporters directly.

The platform demonstrated significant scale during major election cycles. In the 2018 midterms, volunteers contacted over 1 million voters through the platform, and by 2020, volunteers had sent over 100 million text messages. Impactive served over 500 clients nationwide, including Planned Parenthood, the DCCC, SEIU, Community Change, When We All Vote, and Greenpeace.

Operating with a remote team based out of Boston, Impactive has since been acquired.

startups.title: TransAstra Corporation
startups.description: TransAstra develops orbital logistics solutions, including a sunlight-powered propulsion system and asteroid-detecting telescope. YC S21.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.transastra.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/transastra-corporation

TransAstra is a Los Angeles‑based company that has issued five patents and has more than a dozen pending, generating over $5 million in revenue.
Its flagship Omnivore propulsion system powers spacecraft such as the Worker Bee commercial OTV using concentrated sunlight, making it faster, cheaper, and more practical than electric propulsion while being safer and more operationally flexible than legacy chemical systems.
The Sutter Telescope System locates resource‑rich asteroids and orbital debris that existing technologies cannot find, and it can identify dark, fast‑moving objects between Earth and the Moon—an issue that national defense and the Space Force consider critical. Ground‑based observatories already use Sutter, and the company will begin commercial sales of Sutter SDA data next month after tracking dozens of faint moving objects. Once launched, the telescope will be 300,000 times more cost‑effective than any other known design, revolutionizing sense‑making in space.

startups.title: Spaceium Inc
startups.description: Spaceium builds fully automated space stations to refuel and repair spacecraft. YC S24.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://spaceium.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/spaceium-inc

Spaceium builds fully automated space stations to refuel and repair spacecraft. It has secured $86.1 million in binding commercial contracts, $230 million in the pipeline, and $1B in letters of intent, and has successfully tested hardware that will launch next year. The stations store and transfer both cryogenic and non-cryogenic fuels with zero loss, using a proprietary modular robotic arm that can transfer fuel to any spacecraft design. Customers include launch vehicles, orbital transfer vehicles, moon landers, and other spacecraft that benefit from increased payload capacity and extended travel capabilities. Spaceium's long-term vision is to build service hubs along the space superhighway connecting Earth to Moon and Mars, helping humanity become multi-planetary. The company is based in Ottawa, Canada, and operates in the industrial, aviation, and space sectors.

startups.title: Nexa Labs
startups.description: Implantable microchips and AI for cattle monitoring. YC S25.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://nexa.farm/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/nexa-labs

Nexa Labs develops implantable microchips that gather comprehensive biometrics from cattle, surpassing existing market solutions.

The accompanying AI‑driven animal health engine delivers early disease detection, reproductive insights, GPS tracking, and more, enabling farmers to save time and money.

By amassing the world’s largest cattle health dataset, Nexa transforms cattle farming into a science, securing global food supply and boosting economic output. Nexa Labs was acquired in 2025.

startups.title: IMPACT Drones
startups.description: Autonomous interceptor drones that ram hostile targets to protect critical civilian infrastructure. YC S26.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.impact-drones.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/impact-drones

IMPACT Drones develops autonomous interceptor drones designed to defend critical civilian infrastructure, including data centers, power grids, airports, and military bases. The system operates without on-site crew; interceptors are stored in sealed containers at the protected site and launch automatically when sensors detect a hostile drone. The drones use onboard vision for guidance, allowing them to function effectively even when GPS signals are jammed.

The company positions its solution as a cost-effective alternative to legacy air defense systems, which can cost over $1 million per shot against threats that cost only $30,000. IMPACT’s interceptors are designed to cost less than the threat they neutralize and scale with swarm tactics, similar to systems currently downing Shahed drones in Ukraine. By offering a subscription model that includes hardware, reloads, and monitoring, the company provides Air Defense as a Service rather than requiring sites to purchase expensive missile systems.

Based in San Francisco, the company has secured over $180 million in signed letters of intent. It is a two-person team operating in the defense and industrials sectors, focusing on autonomous hardware and swarm robotics.

startups.title: Astranis
startups.description: Builds advanced high-orbit satellites to deliver dedicated, secure telecommunications networks. YC W16.
startups.prose:
**Website:** http://www.astranis.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/astranis

Astranis designs, builds, and operates advanced satellites for high orbits, providing dedicated and secure telecommunications networks across the globe. The company caters to customers with stringent requirements for network visibility, uptime, customization, and data security, including large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military.

Operating out of a 153,000-square-foot headquarters in Northern California, Astranis handles the end-to-end design, manufacturing, and operation of its spacecraft. The company currently has five satellites on orbit with additional launches planned, supporting a commercial contract backlog of over $1 billion.

Founded in the Winter 2016 Y Combinator batch, Astranis employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. To date, it has raised more than $750 million from prominent investors including Andreessen Horowitz, BlackRock, and Fidelity.

startups.title: Exosonic, Inc.
startups.description: Developing supersonic UAVs as a pathway to quiet supersonic flight. YC W20.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://exosonic.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/exosonic-inc

Exosonic, an early-stage aerospace startup based in Los Angeles, developed supersonic adversary air UAVs to support adversary air training missions for commercial and government customers. The company aimed to mature these unmanned vehicles into loyal wingmen or collaborative combat aircraft, with the long-term goal of applying lessons learned to develop quiet supersonic airliners.

Founded in 2019, the team of 14-15 FTEs raised over $4.5M in private capital and $2M in AFWERX funding. They were developing a subscale flight test vehicle designed to demonstrate autonomy and crewed-uncrewed teaming, with a first flight targeted for Q2 2023. Exosonic has since become inactive.

startups.title: Care Weather
startups.description: Collects high-accuracy global weather data using low-cost flat-panel radar satellites. YC W21.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.careweather.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/care-weather

Care Weather operates a unique flat-panel radar satellite designed to capture the highest-accuracy global weather data. The system is vertically integrated, which makes it 1000 times more cost-effective than traditional alternatives, while also generating more solar power and sailing on top of the atmosphere for a closer view of the Earth's surface. This technology enables governments and shipping companies to better adapt to extreme weather events.

The company built and launched the smallest radar satellite ever in just four months. Based in Orem, Utah, Care Weather has secured $35 million worth of letters of intent from clients including the Air Force and various cargo shippers. The startup is backed by investors such as Boost VC, Kickstart Seed Fund, and Y Combinator.

startups.title: Stralis Aircraft
startups.description: Stralis Aircraft builds emission‑free hydrogen electric aircraft. YC W23.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://stralis.aero/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/stralis-aircraft

Stralis Aircraft designs and manufactures hydrogen‑electric airplanes that fly ten times farther than comparable battery‑electric models while offering lower operating costs than conventional fossil‑fuel aircraft. Its first product is a fifteen‑seat aircraft with an 800 km range slated to enter service in 2026 with launch customer Skytrans. The company’s team of four in Brisbane brings over 85 years of aerospace experience, having developed, flight‑tested and certified aircraft at organisations such as Google X, magniX, Heart Aerospace, Ampaire, Airbus, Boeing, Bombardier and Gulfstream. Stralis Aircraft has secured $145 million in letters of intent from seven airlines across the United States, Europe and Australia, underscoring market interest in its zero‑emission solution.

startups.title: Recidiviz
startups.description: Recidiviz builds an open‑source platform that ingests, links, and standardizes criminal‑justice data to enable evidence‑based policy. YC S19.
startups.prose:
**Website:** https://www.recidiviz.org/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/recidiviz

Recidiviz is a non‑profit technology company that creates an open‑source platform for criminal‑justice data. The platform ingests data from disparate silos, links it, standardizes it, and exposes it in usable formats for the ecosystem. It offers products and analyses that help government agencies understand how their justice systems are functioning, set and track progress toward goals, drive evidence‑based improvements to practice and policy, and ensure justice‑impacted individuals reenter their communities safely and quickly. With a team of 120 located in New York City, Recidiviz operates in the government sector as a civic‑tech and GovTech nonprofit.

startups.title: Wavy
startups.description: Wavy builds augmented reality experiences that blend music and art. YC W17.
startups.prose:
**Website:** http://downloadwavy.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/wavy

Wavy creates immersive augmented reality experiences that combine music and visual art, letting users interact with digital content overlaid on the real world. The company operated out of San Francisco and Paris, targeting consumer audiences interested in virtual and augmented reality.

Wavy was acquired, and its current team size is listed as zero, indicating it has been integrated into its acquirer.

startups.title: Francois Chollet
startups.description: Creator of Keras, co-founder of Ndea and ARC Prize. The most credentialed ML researcher to bet against the scaling hypothesis.
startups.prose:
**Twitter:** @fchollet | **LinkedIn:** available

AI researcher at Google for a decade. Creator of **Keras** — the deep learning framework used by millions of practitioners globally, later integrated into TensorFlow as its official high-level API.

In 2019 published a landmark paper arguing that AI benchmarks measure memorisation and pattern matching, not genuine reasoning. Developed the **ARC-AGI benchmark** — tasks requiring visual reasoning and systematic generalisation that LLMs consistently fail.

Co-founded the **ARC Prize Foundation** with [Mike Knoop](./Mike%20Knoop.md) in 2024: $1M annual prizes for AI systems that pass ARC-AGI. The prize has driven significant research attention to the non-scaling approach to AGI.

Left Google in 2025 to co-found [Ndea](./Ndea.md) — an AGI lab pursuing program synthesis. The move was significant: Chollet had spent years publicly arguing that scaling was insufficient, then committed to building the alternative.

startups.title: Mike Knoop
startups.description: Co-founder of Zapier and Ndea. Built a no-code unicorn, then pivoted to AGI research.
startups.prose:
**Twitter:** @mikeknoop | **Website:** mikeknoop.com | **LinkedIn:** available

Co-founded **Zapier** with Wade Foster and Bryan Helmig — the no-code automation platform that became the default glue layer between web apps. Reached $5B valuation as one of the few capital-efficient, bootstrapped unicorns in tech.

Left Zapier after 10+ years to co-found the **ARC Prize Foundation** with [Francois Chollet](./Francois%20Chollet.md): $1M annual prizes for AI systems that pass the ARC-AGI reasoning benchmark.

Co-founded [Ndea](./Ndea.md) with Chollet in 2025. Knoop brings what Chollet lacked: the operational experience of scaling a company from 0 to unicorn — building distributed teams, navigating product decisions, and managing the business challenges that pure researchers underestimate.

The Zapier background is directly relevant: Zapier was built on connecting things that weren't designed to talk to each other. Ndea's program synthesis approach — composing programs from components — maps to the same modularity instinct.

startups.title: Akshay Narisetti
startups.description: Co-founder and CEO of Pocket. Previously built Omi, an open-source AI note-taking device.
startups.prose:
**Twitter:** @AkshayNarisetti | **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/akshaynarisetti

Co-founded [Pocket](./Pocket.md) with [Gabriel Dymowski](./Gabriel%20Dymowski.md).

Previously built **Omi** — an open-source AI note-taking device, which gave Narisetti direct experience with the hardware AI wearable space before Pocket. He knew the failure modes of previous devices (Humane AI Pin, Google Glass) from having shipped in the same category.

The $27M ARR in 5 months is the metric that defines his founding story: hardware velocity at that rate is essentially unprecedented in recent YC history. Series A-level traction at seed stage.

The prior Omi experience mattered: he didn't walk into hardware AI cold. He understood why previous devices failed (wrong form factor, wrong use case, wrong friction level) and designed Pocket around those lessons — smaller, more passive, solving one specific pain rather than replacing the phone.

startups.title: Gabriel Dymowski
startups.description: Co-founder of Pocket. Former CEO and co-founder of DoxyChain, blockchain document infrastructure.
startups.prose:
**Twitter:** @gabrieldymowski | **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/gabrieldymowski

Co-founded [Pocket](./Pocket.md) with [Akshay Narisetti](./Akshay%20Narisetti.md).

Previously served as CEO and co-founder of **DoxyChain** — a blockchain-based document infrastructure company. The DoxyChain background brings enterprise go-to-market experience and the operational discipline of building B2B infrastructure: compliance, security, enterprise sales cycles.

Dymowski's prior CEO experience at DoxyChain is the operational complement to Narisetti's hardware product background. Pocket's challenge post-launch is scaling the supply chain, managing manufacturing, and building the enterprise version of the product — exactly the operational profile Dymowski brings from DoxyChain.

The 30,000 units shipped in 5 months is as much a supply chain achievement as a sales achievement. Hardware at that volume requires supplier relationships, quality control, and logistics infrastructure that takes most hardware startups 12–18 months to build.

startups.title: Aayam Bansal
startups.description: Co-founder of Synthetic Sciences. Published at NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR. Z-Fellow. Founded and sold aisock.
startups.prose:
**Twitter:** @aayambansal | **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/aayambansal/

Co-founded [Synthetic Sciences](./Synthetic%20Sciences.md) with [Ishaan Gangwani](./Ishaan%20Gangwani.md).

Published at **NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AAAI, CVPR** — the top tier of ML and computer vision conferences. At ~18 years old. Previously founded **aisock** (acquired). Patented orthopaedic AI. Built COVID-19 infrastructure used by 50K+ daily users.

**Z-Fellow** (Peter Thiel's fellowship for exceptional young founders). **Emergent Ventures** recipient (Tyler Cowen's grant program for high-potential researchers and entrepreneurs).

The publication record at NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR before turning 18 is essentially unprecedented. These are peer-reviewed venues where most PhD students publish their first paper at 25+. The combination of conference publications and a prior acquisition (aisock) is the founding credential that makes the a16z Scout Fund backing make sense.

startups.title: Ishaan Gangwani
startups.description: Co-founder of Synthetic Sciences. International Olympiad in AI 2025, USACO Platinum top 0.01%. Z-Fellow.
startups.prose:
**LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/ishaan-gangwani-3a7792241/

Co-founded [Synthetic Sciences](./Synthetic%20Sciences.md) with [Aayam Bansal](./Aayam%20Bansal.md).

**International Olympiad in AI 2025** — Honorable Mention (global competition, top competitors from 60+ countries). **USACO Platinum** — top 0.01% of competitive programmers globally. **Z-Fellow** (Peter Thiel's fellowship). **Emergent Ventures** recipient.

USACO Platinum is the metric that the competitive programming community uses to identify exceptional CS talent before degrees exist. Top 0.01% globally means approximately the top 100–150 competitive programmers in the world in his age group.

The IOI-AI and USACO credentials together signal the kind of algorithmic reasoning ability that's directly relevant to building reliable AI agent systems — the [Synthetic Sciences](./Synthetic%20Sciences.md) product requires designing evaluation frameworks and RL environments, which is closer to competitive programming than to prompt engineering.

startups.title: Vivek Nair
startups.description: Co-founder and CEO of Multifactor. Former CIA officer, youngest-ever PhD CS student at UC Berkeley.
startups.prose:
**LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/nair/

Co-founded [Multifactor](./Multifactor.md) with [Colin Roberts](./Colin%20Roberts.md).

**Former CIA officer** and Technical Lead for CIA & DOD elite cyber units. **Ph.D. CS from UC Berkeley** — youngest person ever admitted to the program. NSF Fellow, NPSC Fellow, Hertz Fellow. CIA Exceptional Performance Award.

The security credentials are the product. When Multifactor tells enterprise customers their AI agent authentication is zero-trust and prompt-injection-resistant, the claim is backed by someone who built offensive and defensive cyber operations for the US intelligence community.

Turned down substantial VC term sheets to go through YC — a deliberate choice to access the YC network for a security product that sells to technical buyers who trust YC-pedigree companies.

Raised **$15M**, the largest round in F25. Enterprise customers managing **$7.5B+** in manufacturing supply chains.

startups.title: Colin Roberts
startups.description: Co-founder and CTO of Multifactor. PhD mathematician, former NASA scientist, 10+ years cybersecurity.
startups.prose:
Co-founded [Multifactor](./Multifactor.md) with [Vivek Nair](./Vivek%20Nair.md).

**Ph.D. mathematician**. **Former NASA scientist**. 10+ years of professional cybersecurity experience.

The mathematical background is directly relevant to Multifactor's product: post-quantum cryptography — which Multifactor uses for its authentication system — is a field where mathematical depth determines whether the implementation is actually secure. A PhD mathematician with a decade of applied security experience is the right background for building cryptographic infrastructure that enterprises will stake their security posture on.

The NASA-to-cybersecurity-to-startup trajectory is unusual: deep technical credibility across high-stakes engineering domains, then applied to the commercial problem of securing AI agents. Roberts brings the theoretical rigour that makes Multifactor's security claims verifiable, not just marketed.

Alongside [Vivek Nair](./Vivek%20Nair.md)'s CIA cyber background, Multifactor has arguably the strongest security engineering founding pair in the YC F25/W26 cohort.

startups.title: Tobias Herber
startups.description: Co-founder of Metorial. 3x founder, IEEE best paper award, distributed systems and AI. Vienna.
startups.prose:
**Twitter:** @tobiasherber_ | **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/tobias-herber

Co-founded [Metorial](./Metorial.md) with [Karim Rahme](./Karim%20Rahme.md). Vienna, Austria.

**3x founder**. **IEEE best paper award author** in AI/distributed systems/system software. Previously co-led technology at **Valicit** — an Abu Dhabi-based ticketing startup.

The IEEE best paper background is the technical credibility marker for building the MCP runtime layer: distributed systems reliability, sub-second cold starts, and multi-region failover require exactly the theoretical depth that produces peer-reviewed work on distributed systems.

Chose open source as the distribution strategy — the Metorial runtime is open-source, with the hosted enterprise platform as the revenue layer. The Vercel analogy he uses is precise: Vercel didn't invent deployment, it made Next.js reliable at enterprise scale. Metorial does the same for MCP.

Austria-based founding team in a Valley-dominated ecosystem: the geographic distance from the YC bubble is sometimes cited as a source of product focus rather than distraction.

startups.title: Karim Rahme
startups.description: Co-founder and CEO of Metorial. Building enterprise MCP infrastructure from Vienna.
startups.prose:
**Twitter:** @wen_rahme | **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/karim-rahme

Co-founded [Metorial](./Metorial.md) with [Tobias Herber](./Tobias%20Herber.md). Vienna, Austria.

Background from a top technical high school in Austria. Brings enterprise software and developer infrastructure experience — the combination needed for a product that has to satisfy developer ergonomics (clean MCP connection API) and enterprise requirements (audit logs, compliance, SLAs) simultaneously.

Described in YC materials as building **"Vercel for MCP AI agents."** The CEO role at a 4-person company means Rahme simultaneously handles sales, fundraising, developer relations, and product strategy — the generalist pressure that differentiates the early-stage startup CEO from the specialist technical co-founder.

The Austria location is an operational choice: Vienna has a growing technical talent pool, lower cost base than San Francisco, and proximity to European enterprise customers who are among the earliest MCP adopters in regulated industries.

startups.title: Saksham Aggarwal
startups.description: Co-founder of Cardboard. CS BITS Pilani, ACL researcher, ex-first-engineer at Coinbase-backed PYOR.
startups.prose:
**Twitter:** @sxmawl | **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/sakshamagg27

Co-founded [Cardboard](./Cardboard.md) with [Ishan Sharma](./Ishan%20Sharma.md).

**Education:** CS, BITS Pilani (India's top private engineering university).

**Background:** Co-founder/CTO at Iterate AI (EF-backed). Published research at **ACL** (premier NLP conference). First engineer at **PYOR** (Coinbase and Castle Island Ventures backed). Growth at Sequoia-backed Flint. ~250K monthly views as a content creator.

The ACL publication is an unusual credential for a startup founder: peer-reviewed NLP research at 22 suggests the kind of technical depth that makes the agentic video editing pipeline credible beyond marketing claims.

The PYOR first-engineer role (Coinbase-backed) means Aggarwal has seen what early-stage product engineering looks like at a company with institutional backing — the discipline and speed required before a formal engineering team exists.

startups.title: Ishan Sharma
startups.description: Co-founder and CTO of Cardboard. 4.5 years at HackerRank, built a 5.7M-download app featured on CNET.
startups.prose:
**Twitter:** @ishandeveloper | **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/ishandeveloper

Co-founded [Cardboard](./Cardboard.md) with [Saksham Aggarwal](./Saksham%20Aggarwal.md).

**Background:** ~4.5 years at **HackerRank** (YC S11) leading 0→1 products. Built **Hotspoter** — a consumer app with 5.7M+ downloads, featured on CNET. Expertise in high-performance web systems and browser technology.

The HackerRank tenure (a YC S11 company) gives Sharma the rare combination of having seen how a YC company scales from the inside, and the specific 0→1 product experience of building features at the point where product decisions compound most.

The 5.7M Hotspoter downloads are the consumer distribution signal: Sharma knows how to make something people actually download and use, not just technically impressive demos that don't retain.

The browser technology expertise is what makes Cardboard's browser-native bet credible: high-performance video editing in a browser is a hard systems engineering problem. Most attempts produce laggy, limited experiences. Sharma's background building performant browser systems is the technical unlock.

startups.title: Skyler Chan
startups.description: Solo founder of GRU Space, age 22. Building the first commercial lunar hotel.
startups.prose:
Founded [GRU Space](./GRU%20Space.md) solo at age 22. Currently accepting reservations for lunar hotel stays at $250K–$1M per booking.

Chan's bet is on timing: NASA's Artemis program, SpaceX's Starship, and international lunar programs are converging on a timeline where permanent human lunar presence is plausible within a decade. The hospitality and habitat layer — where humans actually live and work on the Moon — is not being built by NASA or SpaceX; it's a commercial opportunity.

The solo founder structure is notable: [GRU Space](./GRU%20Space.md) requires hardware, aerospace engineering, commercial real estate instincts, hospitality operations, and regulatory navigation. Solo founders in hardware are rare because the surface area is too large for one person. Chan's strategy likely involves extensive use of contractors, aerospace partners, and YC alumni resources.

In the W26 batch, GRU Space stood out for audacity: it's the kind of company that gets immediate press, attracts talent who want to work on a moonshot literally, and generates the Demo Day moments that put YC on news feeds.

startups.title: Prateek Sachan
startups.description: Co-founder of Bolna. Previously scaled products at Zomato, Tata 1MG, BrowserStack, and Atlassian.
startups.prose:
**Twitter:** @xan_ps | **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/prateek-sachan

Co-founded [Bolna](./Bolna.md) with [Maitreya Wagh](./Maitreya%20Wagh.md).

**Background:** Previously built and scaled products at **Zomato** (India's largest food delivery), **Tata 1MG** (health platform), **BrowserStack** (developer testing, $4B valuation), and **Atlassian** (Jira/Confluence).

Four product-building stints at Indian tech companies ranging from startup scale to late-stage unicorn gives Sachan a rare cross-section of Indian enterprise scale-up experience — exactly the customer base that Bolna serves.

The BrowserStack and Atlassian background is particularly relevant: both are developer infrastructure companies with global B2B customers, which gives Sachan the enterprise sales and product development framework to sell Bolna's voice AI into enterprise call centres.

The India-first positioning is founder-market fit: Sachan built products for Indian users at Indian companies. He understands the language diversity, the business communication patterns, and the enterprise sales culture of the Indian market better than any US-based competitor.

startups.title: Maitreya Wagh
startups.description: Co-founder of Bolna. Engineer turned consultant turned AI founder.
startups.prose:
**Twitter:** @maitreya_wagh | **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/maitreya-wagh

Co-founded [Bolna](./Bolna.md) with [Prateek Sachan](./Prateek%20Sachan.md).

Engineer turned consultant turned AI founder — a trajectory that provides both technical depth and business process understanding. The consulting background typically means experience diagnosing inefficiencies in large enterprise workflows, which is exactly what Bolna's voice AI is selling against: manual phone-based processes in Indian enterprises.

The engineer-to-consultant path builds the rare skill of translating between technical capabilities and business problems — Wagh can understand what the model can do and articulate why an enterprise should pay for it. Combined with [Prateek Sachan](./Prateek%20Sachan.md)'s product-building background at Zomato, BrowserStack, and Atlassian, the founding pair covers both the build and the sell.

**500,000+ minutes of calls monthly** is the metric that validates the product-market fit. General Catalyst's **$6.3M** investment (January 2026) reflects institutional conviction in the Indian voice AI market.

startups.title: Lucas Ngoo
startups.description: Founder of Cortex AI. Building the training data layer for embodied AI and robotics.
startups.prose:
Founded [Cortex AI](./Cortex%20AI.md). Raised $6M. Ngoo's background is in computer vision and robotics data — the specific intersection needed to build high-quality embodied AI training datasets that include accurate hand and body pose annotations.

The robotics training data market is structurally similar to what Scale AI built for perception AI in autonomous vehicles: a specialized data collection and annotation pipeline that model teams don't want to build themselves. Ngoo is making the same bet that Alexandr Wang made a decade earlier, but for the embodied AI wave.

The workplace data collection angle is Cortex AI's differentiation: lab data produces policies that work in labs. Factory floor data, collected with workers doing real tasks in real environments, produces policies that generalize to deployment.

startups.title: Magnus Muller
startups.description: Co-founder and CEO of Browser Use. Data Science, ETH Zurich. ML researcher for Cambridge CARES.
startups.prose:
**Twitter:** @mamagnus00 | **LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/magnus-mueller
